criteria.note: Read warp_contract_runner.py in full and drove run()/derive_schema from my own /tmp scripts. derive_schema on a nested payload with lists produced exactly the dotted-path map expected: id=integer, total=number, flag=boolean, meta=null, items=array, items[]=object, items[].sku=string, items[].qty=integer, items[].tags=array, items[].tags[]=string (list-in-list), customer=object, customer.name=string, customer.addr=object, customer.addr.zip=string; the root value itself is not recorded. The producer seam is genuinely used and graded: passing producer=lambda:{good} made a contract with a bad captured block pass, and producer=lambda:{bad} made a contract with a good captured block fail, proving the adopting-repo callable (not the captured fixture) is what gets diffed. Exit codes verified via wrapper: conforming fixture exit 0, drifted fixture exit 1.

Adversarially tried to sneak each drift past the classifier. removed nested field (customer.vip) and removed field inside a list element (items[].qty) both classified removed and breaking. bool where golden=integer, float where golden=integer, float where golden=integer(qty), null where golden=string, and object->array all classified type_changed and breaking. integer under golden=number is NOT drift; number under golden=integer IS drift (JSON-honest). added nested field fails under strict, is tolerated (reported, not breaking) under non-strict; a non-strict contract with a simultaneous removal + type change + addition still fails on the removal and type change while tolerating only the addition. Every case classified correctly.

result records contract name and version (verified name='c', version='v9'). Both an empty golden {} and an absent/None golden return passed:False with error 'contract asserts nothing: an empty golden schema is not proof'; an empty golden with a rich captured payload still fails. A producer that raises returns passed:False with a named 'producer error: <msg>' capture error. No payload + no producer + no captured also fails loud. I also injected passed/conformant/ok=True fields into a payload and confirmed they do NOT force a pass (they are correctly treated as added drift under strict), so there is no claimed-conformant flag path. A vacuous pass is unreachable.

Read the selftest block (lines 1124-1188): it loads the runner and exercises json_type honesty (7 cases), type_satisfies (integer/number both directions, bool), derive_schema for nested objects and list element shapes and root-not-recorded, the diff for clean/removed/type_changed/integer-under-number/added, run() for strict-fails-addition, non-strict-tolerates-addition, non-strict-still-fails-removal, version-recorded, empty-golden error, producer error, producer seam, and both shipped fixtures end to end. python3 scripts/selftest.py -> 328 passed, 0 failed. Proved non-tautological: I replicated the assertions against four mutated copies of the runner in /tmp - type_satisfies always True flipped 4 assertions (type change, both satisfies-direction, all-3-drifts), dropping removed-detection flipped 3 (removed field, non-strict removal, all-3-drifts), making empty golden pass flipped the empty-golden assertion, and making added always breaking flipped the non-strict-tolerates-addition assertion. Baseline flips zero. Wrapper drove both fixtures e2e (conform exit 0, drift exit 1 naming removed/type_changed/added).

Case-insensitive grep for bcengi|dejitech|travelpass|workpass|agentpass|coreconnect|onesim|mvne|dmitry|tripdesk|daybook|stripe|hubspot over runner/fixtures/wrapper/README returned zero matches. Grep for em-dash (U+2014), en-dash (U+2013), and the prose double-hyphen sequence over the same dir all returned no matches. .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical (both sha256 cf8367b3dfdc361e2c1eb5aa5e9d658a4116ba2fdf7ec5e6bd9e7bfeff2dc6a1) and the contract_schema_runner entry declares status: reference, never mechanical. verify.sh reports docs/template-sync/secret/contracts gates all pass, GATE: GREEN bound to c14e406, 0 undeclared.

summary: I independently reran everything at HEAD c14e406 (confirmed == the spec commit) and did not trust the manifest. I recomputed the manifest proof_digest via .warp/validate.proof_digest and got sha256:d2240d9314f0faa3, matching the manifest. verify.sh prints GATE: GREEN bound to c14e406 with 0 undeclared, and python3 scripts/selftest.py reports 328 passed, 0 failed. I read warp_contract_runner.py in full and adversarially exercised its control logic from my own /tmp scripts, trying to refute each acceptance criterion: derive_schema is JSON-honest and recurses objects and list element shapes (including list-in-list) with the root not recorded; the producer seam is genuinely used and is what gets graded; removed and type_changed are always breaking while added is breaking only under strict; bool is not integer or number, integer satisfies a golden number but a number does not satisfy a golden integer, null is its own type, object and array are distinguished; the contract is versioned and cannot pass vacuously (empty golden and producer-error both fail loud, and payload-injected conformance flags do not force a pass). I proved the selftest is non-tautological by mutating four copies of the runner in /tmp and confirming each mutation flips the corresponding selftest assertion, while the unmutated baseline flips nothing. The wrapper drives both shipped fixtures end to end (conform exit 0, drift exit 1 naming removed/type_changed/added). Genericity, dash, and byte-identical capabilities (status: reference, never mechanical) checks all pass. The runner is a distinct golden-snapshot drift detector (json_type/derive_schema/type_satisfies/diff_contract), materially different from WARP-0307's integration runner (check_contract/resolve_path against a live boundary). All five acceptance criteria confirmed with no findings.
